title: walletwise: tenant-aware batch sculptor and quantization guidance
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces tenant-aware batching presets (WalletWise profiles), an interactive quantization guidance doc, and small runtime hooks for safe rollout. No breaking API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers running cost-sensitive tenant workloads repeatedly ask for prescriptive, per-tenant defaults that balance latency SLOs and unit economics without deep runtime tuning. ENG-2314 requested an experimental set of presets for low-traffic tenants; ENG-2407 asked for clearer operator guidance on quantization tradeoffs. This PR introduces the "WalletWise" batch sculptor (a set of tenant-aware batch/cache/quant presets), runtime rollout hooks to enable safe gradual opt-in, and a developer-facing guidance doc that codifies heuristics used by the presets.

What this changes (single-string checklist and detail): 
- Add: walletwise presets under configs/presets/walletwise/* (profiles for tiny, small, medium tenants).
- Add: runtime hook (pkg/runtime/prefill/walletwise.go) that selects a conservative preset when tenant capacity or cost tier is flagged.
- Add: quant guidance doc and interactive checklist (docs/operator/walletwise-quant-guide.md).
- Update: default batcher config merge logic to prefer tenant-specific profiles if present (pkg/config/merge.go).
- Add: telemetry tags for WalletWise decisions (telemetry/metrics.yaml) and sample dashboards (observability/dashboards/walletwise.jsonnet).
- Tests: unit tests for merge behavior and preference fallbacks; a small e2e smoke that runs in the perf-canary suite.

Commits (high-level): 
1) aisha/add-walletwise-presets - add YAML presets for three tenant classes + unit tests for YAML validation.
2) aisha/walletwise-runtime-hook - implement selection hook with feature-flag gated rollout and basic caching integration.
3) aisha/quant-guide - operator doc + examples + small script to validate quant profiles against known-good model artifacts.

Changed areas (high level, illustrative): 
- configs/presets/walletwise/
  - tiny.yaml (prefill: enabled, batch_size_target: 1-4, kv_cache_policy: conservative, quant_profile: q4_8_safe)
  - small.yaml (prefill: enabled, batch_size_target: 4-16, kv_cache_policy: balanced, quant_profile: q4_0_mixed)
  - medium.yaml (prefill: enabled, batch_size_target: 16-64, kv_cache_policy: aggressive, quant_profile: q3_4_perf)
- pkg/runtime/prefill/walletwise.go 
  - adds SelectWalletwiseProfile(tenantMeta, workloadSig) and unit tests 
  - safe fallback to global defaults when instrumented signals are missing
- pkg/config/merge.go 
  - updates merge logic to consult tenant presets before applying global heuristics
- docs/operator/walletwise-quant-guide.md 
  - step-by-step: sample evaluation harness commands, token/latency tradeoff table, guidance for fallback quant profiles 
- observability/dashboards/walletwise.jsonnet 
  - new dashboard showing per-tenant unit cost delta and prefill hit-rate

Review conversation (abridged and inline): 
- Marco Ruiz (request changes): "Nice approach. Two concerns: ensure the runtime hook does not introduce contention on the prefill path, and add a canary-only env var so we can test without hitting production tenants."
- Aisha (author): "Thanks Marco — hook uses non-blocking read path and writes decisions to a per-tenant cache with TTL. Added WALLETWISE_CANARY_ONLY flag (defaults to true in rollout). See pkg/runtime/prefill/walletwise.go: lines 38-76 for the gating logic."
- Liang Chen (nit + approval after fix): "Please add a unit test that simulates missing instrumentation and verify fallback to global default. Otherwise LGTM."
- Aisha: "Added TestSelectProfile_missingSignals in runtime/prefill/walletwise_test.go; updated description."
- Sofia Morales (security review): "Confirm no tenant secrets or KMS calls are introduced. Also request an operations playbook for rollback."
- Aisha: "No secrets/KMS added; playbook added under docs/operator/rollback-playbooks/walletwise-rollback.md."

CI and validation: 
- CI matrix: unit, lint, integration(perf-canary). First run: unit/lint passed, integration flaky: perf-canary-smoke timed out on one run (timeout in the e2e harness). I re-ran the canary job; second run passed. All gates green before merge.

Rollout plan and safety: 
- Feature flag WALLETWISE_CANARY_ONLY true by default. Ops can flip to tenant opt-in via tenant metadata, then to global opt-in after monitoring.
- Telemetry emits walletwise.decision.{tiny,small,medium} and walletwise.fallback.* to detect misclassification.
- Added SLO guard: if prefill hit-rate < 30% and 95th p99 latency regresses > 10% for two consecutive 1h windows, an automated rollback signal will be emitted to alerting.

Docs and operator guidance summary: 
- docs/operator/walletwise-quant-guide.md: contains a short script to run the quant-sanity-check on a model artifact, recommended thresholds (quality drop <= 2% on the standard eval set), and a small table mapping quant_profile -> expected token throughput improvements.
- docs/operator/rollback-playbooks/walletwise-rollback.md: quick steps to disable the feature flag, clear tenant cache, and revert runtime via a single staging rollback script.

Related work and alternatives considered: 
- Considered embedding presets in the console UI; deferred to follow-up so that operators can iterate on YAML first.
- Evaluated automatic re-quantization runbooks but rejected for this change due to higher risk (separate PR planned).

Merge outcome: 
- Merged via squash on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Liang and Sofia and after CI green on second canary run. Merge commit message included a pointer to ENG-2314 and ENG-2407.

Follow-ups (tracking): 
- ENG-2460: Console UI for WalletWise presets and per-tenant overrides.
- ENG-2483: Automated quant revalidation pipeline (separate RFC).
- PM: Add customer-facing release note and a short blog outlining cost/latency outcomes observed in canary tenants.

Notes for reviewers or future readers: 
- This PR aims to be conservative by default — default presets bias toward preserving latency SLOs for tiny tenants while delivering cost savings for medium tenants. Operators should treat WalletWise as a starter kit: observe telemetry, adjust batch_size_target, and iterate on quant_profile conservatively.

If anything is unclear, see the inline comments on the runtime hook and the test coverage file runtime/prefill/walletwise_test.go for typical failure modes.
